title: Enivré par le pouvoir  (Intoxicated by Power)

segments.t: Backstage before the opening ceremony, wealthy businessman Gillieres corners Juliette Binoche. He confesses an overwhelming attraction, but Juliette uses her quick wit to outsmart him. Let's listen to the scene in French first.
Je voulais te souhaiter bonne chance.
Tu es magnifique, tu me rends fou!
Le pouvoir que tu as m'enivre!
Merci Jean-Denis, mais sois bien raisonnable.
Tu ne veux pas de moi?
Si, mais pas de cette manière.
Je ne veux rien partager.
Donne-moi ton téléphone portable, voyons!
Pourquoi veux-tu mon téléphone portable?
Nous allons appeler ta femme Caroline!
Attends, parlons plutôt après la fête.
Oui, après la grande cérémonie officielle.
C'est bien plus sage ainsi.
À tout à l'heure, cher ami!
Let's examine how Juliette skillfully defuses the advances of Gillieres step by step.
Je voulais te souhaiter bonne chance.
'I wanted to wish you good luck.' Using past 'I wanted' instead of blunt 'I want' softens an approach in French, capped by 'good chance' for 'good luck.'
Tu es magnifique, tu me rends fou!
'You are magnificent, you drive me crazy!' Where English says 'drive me crazy,' French uses 'render'—literally 'you me render crazy!'
Le pouvoir que tu as m'enivre!
'The power you have intoxicates me!' Built from 'in' plus 'drunk,' that dramatic final word in French literally means 'makes me drunk'!
Merci Jean-Denis, mais sois bien raisonnable.
'Thank you Jean-Denis, but be quite sensible.' Again irregular command 'be!' pairs with 'reasonable'—a cognate that means 'sensible' in French.
Tu ne veux pas de moi?
'Do you not want me?' Notice 'want of me' adding 'of' in the negative whenever 'want' means desiring a person romantically in French.
Si, mais pas de cette manière.
'Yes, but not this way.' Crucial distinction in French: to contradict a negative question with 'yes, I do!', you MUST use the special rebuttal 'yes' rather than ordinary 'yes'!
Je ne veux rien partager.
'I do not want to share anything.' In the negative, 'nothing' tucks BEFORE 'to share'—so word for word Juliette says 'I not want nothing to-share.'
Donne-moi ton téléphone portable, voyons!
'Give me your cell phone, come on!' Literally 'telephone portable' for a mobile phone, followed by 'let's see!'—a lively nudge meaning 'come on!'
Pourquoi veux-tu mon téléphone portable?
'Why do you want my cell phone?' Inverting 'want-you' after 'why' in French shows Gillieres stammering in sudden panic over his 'telephone portable.'
Nous allons appeler ta femme Caroline!
'We are going to call your wife Caroline!' In French, the exact same word means both 'woman' and 'wife'—context plus 'your' makes 'your wife' unmistakable.
Attends, parlons plutôt après la fête.
'Wait, let us talk rather after the party.' Group 'talk' without 'we' means 'let's talk' in French, softened right away by 'rather.'
Oui, après la grande cérémonie officielle.
'Yes, after the big official ceremony.' Notice short 'big' before 'ceremony' and longer 'official' right after—a classic sandwich in French!
C'est bien plus sage ainsi.
'It is much wiser this way.' Here that familiar description returns in its root sense and means 'wise,' boosted by 'well more' for 'much wiser.'
À tout à l'heure, cher ami!

'See you later, dear friend!' Literally 'until all at the hour,' this classic farewell in French is ONLY for seeing someone again later the very same day! Now let's listen to the whole scene once more from start to finish.
Je voulais te souhaiter bonne chance.
Tu es magnifique, tu me rends fou!
Le pouvoir que tu as m'enivre!
Merci Jean-Denis, mais sois bien raisonnable.
Tu ne veux pas de moi?
Si, mais pas de cette manière.
Je ne veux rien partager.
Donne-moi ton téléphone portable, voyons!
Pourquoi veux-tu mon téléphone portable?
Nous allons appeler ta femme Caroline!
Attends, parlons plutôt après la fête.
Oui, après la grande cérémonie officielle.
C'est bien plus sage ainsi.
À tout à l'heure, cher ami!
Juliette Binoche masterfully defuses an uncomfortable confrontation with humor and sharp presence of mind. See you next time!
Au revoir!
